http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/11/belar.text: Aliaksandr Milinkevich, the physicist-turned-politician who united Belarus’s opposition forces to challenge Aliaksandr Lukashenka in the 2006 presidential election, has died at the age of 79.His death was announced on Tuesday.Milinkevich underwent a complicated operation to remove a blood clot from his carotid artery last year. He spent a prolonged period in critical condition and later underwent extensive rehabilitation.From academia to politicsMilinkevich was born in 1947, in Grodno, Belarus. After graduating from the faculty of physics and mathematics at the Grodno Pedagogical Institute, he worked as a teacher at a local school. He later earned a PhD and became an associate professor at the same institution.He went on to author dozens of academic works on quantum electronics and laser technology, as well as on Belarusian culture, art, education and more.Around the time of the Soviet Union's collapse, he moved into the public sector, and from 1990 to 1996, he served as deputy chair of the Grodno city executive committee.In 2001, he headed the campaign headquarters of Belarusian presidential candidate Semyon Domash, and five years later he ran for the presidency himself.A pro-European challengerIn 2005, Milinkevich was chosen as the candidate of the opposition democratic forces, which stood as a united front against the Lukashenka regime. A pro-European vision for Belarus became a defining feature of his campaign.The election campaign was marked by intense pressure on the opposition, including threats of criminal prosecution, disinformation campaigns in pro-government media, and arrests of opposition activists at rallies.In the end, according to the official figures, Lukashenka took 83% of the vote, with Milinkevich receiving 6%. Both in the United States and in Europe, doubts remained over the reliability of the results and the legitimacy of Lukashenka's third term in office.That same year, Milinkevich received the European Parliament’s Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought.After the unprecedentedly harsh suppression of protests in Belarus in 2020, he left the country and lived in exile with his family.He became an adviser to opposition leader in exile Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya and the founder of the "Free Belarusian University," with its headquarters in Warsaw.'Return to the European family'Immediately after the election, Milinkevich founded the civic movement "For Freedom," which he continued to lead for another decade.The movement championed European values and advocated for the development of civil society in Belarus, free and fair elections, democratic rights and European standards of living."By our mentality, traditions, history, culture and language, we are Europeans. For me, it has never been a matter of choosing which way we should go, east or west. For me it has been about returning to the European family from which we were forcibly taken into an empire," he said in one interview.For Milinkevich, the issue was ultimately existential - "about whether Belarusians will continue to exist in our own country. The master of the Kremlin does not recognise as a nation not only Ukrainians, but us as well," he said.'A man of exceptional dignity'Tsikhanouskaya has expressed her condolences to Milinkevich's family."A man of exceptional dignity, a kind soul and a brilliant mind, he was a true point of reference for many of us. For me, Aliaksandr was a source of support and wisdom, whose advice I always valued deeply," she wrote in a post on X."His devotion to Belarus, our language and culture, and his ability to unite and support people in the most difficult moments will remain with us," she added.President of the European Parliament Roberta Metsola also responded to the news on social media, writing: "Aliaksandr Milinkevich dedicated his life to the fight for democracy in Belarus.""His courage and legacy will stay with us. Europe continues to stand with the people of Belarus," Metsola said.In a 2006 interview, Milinkevich told Euronews: “The humiliation people feel when living in fear, the violation of their dignity — this, I believe, is the root cause of all Belarus’s problems."For years, he watched as Lukashenka’s regime crushed even the smallest expressions of dissent, stamping out any signs of resistance in Belarusian society. Yet he never lost his optimism. In fact, he said his faith in change had grown stronger after the events of 2020."We have experience, we had the fantastic year 2020, when everyone contributed to the Belarusian spirit and the desire to defend their 'self', truth, freedom. After 2020, I am an absolute optimist, because a completely different nation was born. People overcame their fear," he said.

https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/boris-joh.text: Rebecca Robinson Updated Sun, September 13, 2026 at 4:26 PM UTC 4 Boris Johnson had to be evacuated from Ukraine. (Image: Getty) Boris Johnson has broken his silence after he had to be evacuated from Ukraine to escape a Russian drone attack. The former Prime Minister was travelling back from a security conference in Kyiv when Moscow struck a train minutes behind his, leaving him scrambling to get over the border into Poland. He called Vladimir Putin "warped" for his military's attack on civilian infrastructure, and slammed the Government for not giving seized Russian assets to Ukraine. He said: "I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning. Johnson was speaking at a security conference in Kyiv. (Image: Getty) "What we can say for sure is that this is the kind of random and senseless attack Ukrainians are enduring every day - even on civilian railways. "So far Putin has been responsible for the deaths of 1700 staff of Ukrzaliznytsia - Ukrainian Railways. They and their daily passengers are absolutely heroic. "When are we going to give them the air defences they need? Why won't we unfreeze Putin's cash and give it to Ukraine? There is more than €140 billion in a Belgian bank account - and about £10 billion in London. Britain could show a lead. "The Ukrainians are going to win - that much was clear from the last three days in their wonderful country. But we will get this dreadful war over much faster if we all get serious and give them what they need and deserve." The privately chartered train carrying Mr Johnson and other dignitaries was stopped and evacuated at around 5am local time on Sunday, according to reports. Another nearby train was hit as Russia launched an assault on the Ukraine-Poland border. Former Swedish prime minister Carl Bildt was among those on the train with Mr Johnson. "This wasn't our train [that was hit], but the one just minutes after us by the [Polish] border crossing," he said. "It was evacuated as the [Russian] drone approached and no one was hurt. Our train just had an evacuation warning but could proceed to Dorohusk. The [Russian] attacks against [Ukraine] are intensifying." Günter Sautter, foreign and security policy advisor to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, was also on the "special train", as well as European security advisers, members of the German Bundestag, diplomats and scientists, reports Der Spiegel . It is thought they had been attending the Yalta European Strategy (YES) in the Ukrainian capital. Everybody was unharmed, and the train continued with its journey after no more drones were detected, reports say.
